APPLICATION OF EL PASO                          §        BEFORE THE STATE OFFICE
ELECTRIC COMPANY FOR APPROVAL                   §
OF A HIGH LOAD FACTOR LARGE                     §                       OF
POWER SERVICE TARIFF                            §
                                                §       ADMINISTRATIVE HEARINGS

                    EL PASO ELECTRIC COMPANY'S RESPONSE TO
                     TEXAS INDUSTRIAL ENERGY CONSUMERS’
                        SECOND REQUEST FOR INFORMATION
                              QUESTION NO. TIEC 2-1

TIEC 2-1:

      Referring to page 3 of the Application:

      a.    Please define the term “advanced manufacturing customers” and identify examples

            of types of customers that would qualify under EPE’s definition. In responding,

            please provide EPE’s reasoning for selecting that definition.

      b.    Please explain how EPE selected 85% annual load factor as a threshold for eligibility

            under the proposed tariff.



RESPONSE:

      a.    Advanced manufacturing is the production of physical goods using highly automated,

            digitally integrated, precision, or technologically innovative processes, or the

            manufacture of technologically advanced products or materials, typically involving

            substantial application of computing, robotics, advanced materials, process controls,

            or other emerging technologies.

                   This definition is broad enough to encompass semiconductors, batteries,

            aerospace, advanced energy technologies and precision manufacturing, while

            avoiding the tendency to label virtually every modern industrial or commercial

            facility “advanced manufacturing.” Customers meeting this definition also share

            electrical characteristics with data centers, such as –

            •     Large, concentrated loads — semiconductor fabricators and battery plants can

                  reach hundreds of MW.

            •     High load factors — many operate continuously or nearly continuously.

            •     High reliability/power-quality requirements — voltage excursions or

                  momentary interruptions can destroy work-in-process or disrupt highly

                  controlled processes.

            •     Long-lived infrastructure requirements — transmission, substations and

                  generation may need to be developed specifically to accommodate a facility.

            •     Rapid load ramps — a facility can add several hundred MW much faster than

                  traditional industrial or manufacturing load.

      b.    EPE elected the 85% threshold for the proposed high-load factor tariff to establish a

            consistent load profile across eligible customers. EPE’s existing large load rate class

            has an average load factor on the order of 60%-70%, with customers significantly

            smaller than what is expected with data centers. The threshold is intended to

            encompass inference data center characteristics while also capturing AI-training and

            advanced manufacturing. Experience going forward may inform a revised threshold

            or potentially require addition of another class for very large customers not meeting

            the 85% threshold.
